summary: Eltrombopag is an orally active thrombopoietin receptor agonist used for chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) refractory to other therapies, thrombocytopenia in chronic hepatitis C to permit interferon-based therapy, and severe aplastic anemia. It increases platelet counts by stimulating megakaryopoiesis. It carries a BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity (and for hepatic decompensation in hepatitis C patients on interferon/ribavirin), so liver tests must be monitored. The goal is to reach a platelet count that prevents bleeding (at least 50 x 10^9/L), not to normalize counts, because excessive elevation increases thrombotic risk. Eltrombopag chelates polyvalent cations (iron, calcium, aluminum, magnesium, zinc), so it must be separated from food, antacids, dairy, and mineral supplements. The starting dose is reduced in patients of East/Southeast Asian ancestry and in hepatic impairment.
indications: Thrombocytopenia in adults and pediatric patients 1 year and older with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who have had an insufficient response to corticosteroids, immunoglobulins, or splenectomy
Thrombocytopenia in patients with chronic hepatitis C to allow the initiation and maintenance of interferon-based therapy
Severe aplastic anemia (first-line in combination with standard immunosuppressive therapy, or refractory disease)

admin: Take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal) or with a meal low in calcium (<=50 mg)
Separate from polyvalent-cation products (antacids, dairy, calcium/iron/magnesium/zinc supplements) by at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after the dose
Check liver function before and during treatment per the schedule
Titrate the dose to the lowest level that maintains a platelet count that avoids bleeding, not to normalize counts
Obtain baseline and periodic eye examinations (cataract risk)
moa: Eltrombopag is a small-molecule, non-peptide agonist of the thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor (c-Mpl). It binds the transmembrane domain of the receptor at a site distinct from endogenous TPO and initiates JAK/STAT and MAPK signaling, stimulating proliferation and differentiation of megakaryocytes from bone marrow progenitor cells and thereby increasing platelet production. Because it does not compete with TPO for the same binding site, it can act additively with endogenous TPO. In aplastic anemia it also stimulates more primitive hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, supporting trilineage hematopoietic recovery.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to eltrombopag or any component
relative: Chronic hepatitis C on interferon/ribavirin (risk of hepatic decompensation)
Pre-existing hepatic impairment (reduce dose; increased hepatotoxicity risk)
Conditions predisposing to bone marrow reticulin fibrosis
monitor: CBC with platelet count and peripheral smear

preg: There are insufficient human data; animal studies showed embryolethality and reduced fetal weights at exposures above the human ITP exposure. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Females of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 7 days after the last dose.
lact: Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment with eltrombopag and for a period after, because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is defined; use with caution and monitor closely in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: In ITP and refractory severe aplastic anemia, reduce the initial dose to 25 mg once daily in patients with any degree of hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A, B, or C); for chronic hepatitis C thrombocytopenia no starting-dose adjustment is needed. Eltrombopag itself can cause hepatotoxicity, so monitor liver tests closely.

major: Polyvalent cation products (iron, calcium, aluminum, magnesium, selenium, zinc - in antacids, dairy, mineral supplements) - chelation markedly reduces absorption; separate by >=2 hours before or 4 hours after
Interferon/ribavirin in hepatitis C - increased risk of hepatic decompensation
moderate: Statins and other OATP1B1/BCRP substrates (e.g., rosuvastatin) - increased exposure; reduce rosuvastatin dose by ~50% and monitor
Drugs metabolized by or transported via OATP1B1/BCRP - monitor for increased exposure
minor: No dosage adjustment needed with lopinavir/ritonavir, boceprevir, or telaprevir
interactions.food: High-calcium meals and dairy substantially reduce absorption; take without food or with a low-calcium (<=50 mg) meal.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol, which adds to the risk of hepatotoxicity.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes elevations in liver enzymes and bilirubin; monitor with scheduled LFTs.

serious: Thromboembolic and thrombotic events (including portal vein thrombosis)
rare: Severe rebound thrombocytopenia and bleeding after discontinuation
emergency: Acute thrombosis (e.g., MI, stroke, pulmonary embolism, portal vein thrombosis)

monitoring: CBC with platelet count and peripheral smears - weekly until stable platelet count, then monthly
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) before treatment, every 2 weeks during dose adjustment, then monthly
Eye examination at baseline and periodically (cataracts)
Platelet counts weekly for 4 weeks after discontinuation (rebound thrombocytopenia/bleeding)
counsel: Take this medicine on an empty stomach or with a low-dairy/low-calcium meal
Keep it at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after antacids, dairy, and iron/calcium/magnesium/zinc supplements
Attend all blood tests - your platelet count and liver tests must be checked regularly
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or right-sided belly pain (liver problems)
Get urgent help for chest pain, breathlessness, leg swelling, or weakness/numbness (possible clots)
Do not stop suddenly without your doctor - your platelets can drop sharply and cause bleeding
pk: Platelet rise typically begins after about 1-2 weeks of dosing
Plasma Tmax ~2-6 hours after an oral dose
Approximately 21-32 hours in healthy subjects (longer in ITP patients)
Once-daily dosing; platelet effect reverses within ~2 weeks of stopping
pearls: BOXED WARNING: hepatotoxicity, and hepatic decompensation in hepatitis C patients on interferon/ribavirin - monitor LFTs
Treat to a SAFE platelet count (>=50 x 10^9/L), not to normalize - over-correction increases thrombosis risk
Chelates polyvalent cations - separate from food, antacids, dairy, iron/calcium/magnesium/zinc by hours
Reduce the starting dose in patients of East/Southeast Asian ancestry and in hepatic impairment
Monitor for cataracts and bone marrow reticulin fibrosis on long-term use
Check platelets weekly for ~4 weeks after stopping - rebound thrombocytopenia and bleeding can occur
missed: If you miss a dose, take only one dose that day as soon as you remember; do not take two doses in one day. Resume your usual once-daily schedule the next day.
overdose: Overdose may raise the platelet count excessively, increasing the risk of thrombotic/thromboembolic complications. There is no specific antidote and eltrombopag is not expected to be removed by dialysis (highly protein bound). Consider oral administration of a polyvalent-cation preparation (such as a calcium- or aluminum-containing antacid) to chelate and limit absorption; monitor platelet counts closely and treat thrombosis as it arises.
